Jess (CS Ops): Heads up — drafting a one-page customer triage card for early onboarding issues around caching/batching/streaming. Goal: a <2min checklist CS can send during kickoff. Thoughts?
Mike (Eng Run): Love it. Can you include a short 'when to escalate to eng' section? e.g., persistent 5xxs, queue build-up, warm pool failures.
Sofia (PM): Also add a quick asks list for customers to bring to kickoff: concurrency targets, sample prompt sizes, expected daily tokens, any PII constraints.
Anil (SRE): +1. Suggest adding quick commands to check warm pool health and recent error rates. sample query:
Anil (SRE): ```
# check warm pool utilization
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/internal/pools/warm?tenant=ACME
# get error rates
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://api.redwood.ai/telemetry/errors?service=inference&window=1h
```
Jess (CS Ops): Nice. I drafted a minimal template — short bullets, triage steps, and an external feedback link. Pasting below.
Jess (CS Ops): 1) Playback: confirm customer can stream tokens and that streaming flag is enabled. 2) Prefill: confirm prefill requests sent during warmup. 3) Batching: confirm client's batch strategy (single-request vs client-side queue). 4) Fallbacks: ensure canary fallback to smaller quantized model is configured. 5) Escalation: what logs to attach (request id, model, seq len, deploy-id). 6) Renewal risk: if >2 failed go-lives or >3 days unresolved, tag as 'at-risk' and loop AM/Sales.
Sofia (PM): Can we include a one-line "customer shareable" blurb? e.g., "To minimize latency, we recommend prepopulating warm pools with 5–10 representative prompts and enabling streaming."
Mike (Eng Run): I can add a compact section on server-side heuristics: prefix caching TTLs, preferred batch sizes per model family, and a note on KV cache hit rates.
Jess (CS Ops): Here's the feedback capture link I'm planning to use: https://forms.goo.gl/example-feedback (placeholder). Also linking the draft doc: https://confluence/research/cs-triage-card (placeholder).
Anil (SRE): One more: add a quick recovery step for surge: "scale burst to Dedicated for 1h and enable throttled queueing client-side" — saves a lot of back-and-forth.
Mike (Eng Run): +1. Will add a 3-line snippet customers can drop in: `max_batch_size=8; prefer_stream=true; prefill_on_start=true`
deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: cs-triage-card v0.1 -> prod :tada:
Jess (CS Ops): Could everyone glance and drop :eyes: or :thumbsup: if OK? I want to ship this as a CS template today.
Sofia (PM): :eyes:
Mike (Eng Run): :thumbsup:
Anil (SRE): :thumbsup: small edit: change TTL note to 'adaptive TTL (30s-5m)'.
Jess (CS Ops): done, pushed. I'll send to the enablement channel and include a short recording demo.
Mike (Eng Run): Thank you — will add the model-family table tomorrow.
Jess (CS Ops): Nice work team. Saving this thread as the canonical quick-triage template. Closing once we've got public link + short recording.
